subject: Future Tech
title: Materials by Quantum Design
description: A quick, practical guide to Materials by Quantum Design.

hook.text: Superconductors, catalysts, and battery materials all depend on quantum effects too complex for classical models.

buildup.text: Finding a room-temperature superconductor would transform energy grids and transport. The search is decades old.

discovery.text: Quantum computers could simulate electron behavior in new materials, predicting properties before anything is built.

twist.text: Each breakthrough material could reshape an industry, yet the simulations need thousands of reliable qubits.

climax.text: Early hybrid experiments already optimize small catalysts. Larger molecules are the next frontier for quantum.

punchline.text: Designing atoms could replace mining them.

quiz.question: Why is quantum simulation valuable for materials science?
options: It predicts properties by modeling electrons
